label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Many of you have tagged me under the post @Kavya put up about founders hiring from their own cohort. Yes, it is about me. She is a good friend and I am not here to fight with her, so I will say my side once, here, and leave it.

First, the part I got wrong. Two engineers from SitterNest joined DabbaDost on 3 November. I knew where they worked from the day they applied. I should have called Kavya before any offer went out. I messaged her only after the second offer was accepted, which is too late to call it a heads up. That is on me. Kavya, I am sorry.

Now the parts that are not correct.

Nobody from DabbaDost DMed anyone. We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 September, open to all. The first engineer applied on his own on 19 September. The second came about two weeks later as his referral.

The hike was 22% over their current CTC, not 40. I am putting the number here only because 40 is the one going around.

On ESOPs, we do have a pool. It is small, but it is real and it has been on paper since January. Nothing was promised that does not exist.

I am not naming the two of them, and I request everyone in the comments to do the same. They applied for a job. They did not ask for any of this.

About Kavya. Before our demo day in March, our Razorpay webhooks were a mess, and she sat with me in the Koramangala office till 1am fixing them. It was not her company and not her problem. I have never forgotten that. I understand why she is upset. Losing two engineers together is hard for a small team, and hearing it late from a friend makes it worse.

This will keep happening to all of us. Foundry91 cohort 4 has 11 startups and we all hire from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. So one suggestion for the batch: if you are interviewing someone from another cohort company, give that founder a heads up before the offer goes out. This is not about asking permission. People are free to work wherever they want. It is only so that no founder finds out afterwards, the way Kavya did. I will be the first to follow it.

Kavya, coffee or a call, any day this week, whenever you are okay with it. I will come wherever suits you.

---

That is about 425 words and roughly 2,300 characters, so it fits both limits. Two things to check before you post:

- **The tag:** retype @Kavya on LinkedIn and pick her profile so it becomes a real tag.
- **The WhatsApp:** I left out that she blue-ticked your message, because in public it would read as a dig at her.
